props.title: Weddings and ceremonies, photographed as they happen
props.text: We are two photographers from Patan. We do not stage the swayambar or ask the priest to wait. We stay close, keep quiet, and give you the day back as it was.

props.heading: Portraits of the people who hold a family together
props.body:
Every wedding has someone who has been to sixty of them. We always ask for twenty minutes with the grandparents, away from the stage, in good light.

We also photograph elders at home, on their own or with the family, for the wall and for the day they are not with you any more.

items.q: How far ahead should we book?
items.a: For Mangsir and Falgun saits, three to six months. We take one wedding a day, and the best dates go first.

items.q: Can we have all the photographs, unedited?
items.a: We give you every photograph worth keeping, edited. Blurred and blinking frames are deleted, which is kinder to everyone.

pages.title: Weddings
pages.seoTitle: Wedding photography in Kathmandu, Patan and Bhaktapur
pages.seoDescription: Mehendi, swayambar, bihe and reception, photographed by two photographers from Patan. Packages from Rs 85,000, with albums printed in Kathmandu.

props.title: Every ritual, and everything between them
props.text: A Nepali wedding is three days of small moments with a few big ones in the middle. We photograph the tika, the tears and the dancing, and nobody has to stand still for us.

image.alt: A bride in red with her hennaed hands raised

props.eyebrow: From Rs 85,000 a day in the valley

image.alt: Hennaed hands and gold bangles on an orange sari

items.title: Mehendi
items.text: Usually at home, usually loud. We photograph the henna going on, the aunts singing and the bride trying not to smudge anything for four hours.

image.alt: A couple exchanging garlands in front of red and gold drapes

items.title: Swayambar
items.text: The garlands, the rings and the first look. We stay near the stage but not on it, and move with the families rather than asking them to move for us.

image.alt: A bride checking her reflection in a mirror

items.title: Bihe
items.text: From getting ready at dawn to the sindoor, the kanyadan and the doli. Rojina stays with the bride; Sagun stays with the groom and the janti.

props.heading: How a family session goes
props.body:
We arrive, have tea and talk for twenty minutes before the camera comes out. Children stop performing after about half an hour, which is when the good photographs start.

Wear what you would wear to a family puja. Avoid matching outfits; they look better on a calendar than on a wall.

props.title: Grandparents visiting for Dashain?
props.text: Book an elders’ portrait for the week they are with you.

pages.title: About
pages.seoTitle: About Tole Studio: Sagun and Rojina Shakya, Patan
pages.seoDescription: Two photographers from Kumbheshwor, Patan, working together since 2073. How we started, how we work, and where to see more.

props.title: Two photographers, one tole
props.text: Sagun grew up above his father’s photo shop in Mangal Bazaar, printing passport photos after school. Rojina studied sociology and still takes notes at every wedding.

image.alt: A woman in a red and black sari in a carved Newari doorway

items.text: And the studio becomes two people who photograph every wedding together.

items.title: Albums printed in Kathmandu
